message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance as international hubs:

| Airport (IATA) | City / State | Passenger Traffic (2022) | Notes |
|----------------|--------------|--------------------------|-------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL)** | Atlanta, GA | ~107 million | Largest airport in the world by passenger numbers; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| **Los Angeles International Airport (LAX)** | Los Angeles, CA | ~88 million | Key gateway to Asia and Latin America; hub for American Airlines and United. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD)** | Chicago, IL | ~84 million | One of the busiest airports in North America; hub for United and American. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW)** | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | ~70 million | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| **Denver International Airport (DEN)** | Denver, CO | ~63 million | Hub for United and Southwest; known for its distinctive peaked roof. |
| **John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)** | New York, NY | ~61 million | Primary hub for United and American; major gateway to Europe. |
| **San Francisco International Airport (SFO)** | San Francisco, CA | ~58 million | Hub for United and a key gateway to Asia. |
| **Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA)** | Seattle, WA | ~56 million | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| **McCarran International Airport (LAS)** | Las Vegas, NV | ~55 million | Major hub for Southwest; high volume of leisure travelers. |
| **Orlando International Airport (MCO)** | Orlando, FL | ~54 million | Major hub for United; serves many leisure travelers to theme parks. |

These airports are among the busiest in the U.S., handling tens of millions of passengers each year and serving as major hubs for both domestic and international flights.
